INTERRUPTION ANALYTICS  /  CATEGORICAL ASSOCIATION STUDY

Where equipment interruptions actually concentrate — and why.

A correspondence-analysis and multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) study of 48,810 logged interruption events across 53 machine groups, mapping how Machine, Reason Code, Product Code and Interruption Level relate to one another.

How to read every table below. Every statistic in this report — chi-square, Cramer's V, MCA inertia, lift, and map distance — is computed from the count of interruption events in each category combination, not from how long any interruption lasted. Interruption Level (Low / Medium / High / Critical) is itself just one more category attached to each event, counted the same way as Machine Group, Reason Code or Product Code. The "Interruption time" column shown in the combination tables is included purely for operational context and did not feed into any of the association statistics.

01 — THE INTERRUPTION LANDSCAPE

A handful of machine groups carry most of the interruptions

Ranking the 53 machine groups by total logged interruption time, the top 12 alone account for 79% of all 1,915 interruption-hours in the dataset. Bar length is total interruption time; the annotation is the share of that group's events classified at the Critical interruption level.

Read this as an Andon board. Wire-bond machines (WB-KS, WB-ASM) and die-attach/eutectic stations (DS-DISCO, DA-ESEC, DA-ASM) together log over 4,000 interruption-hours — more than half of the entire dataset. Several smaller groups (HDLR-MULTITEST, CLNR-MARCH, OVEN-ATV, HDLR-MCT, HDLR-IN2) have 99%+ of their interruptions classified as Critical level — almost none of their stoppages are minor, which points to single severe failures rather than routine micro-stops.
02 — PAIRWISE ASSOCIATIONS (CORRESPONDENCE ANALYSIS)

How strongly is each pair of variables related?

Before looking at three-way structure, each pair of categorical variables was tested independently with a chi-square test on the interruption-count contingency table, then mapped with classical Correspondence Analysis (CA). Cramer's V measures the strength of association (0 = none, 1 = perfect); the table beneath each map lists that file's top 5 most statistically associated cells (largest standardized residuals).

Machine Group × Reason Code

V = 0.682
Strong association
χ² = 1,179,330 · dof = 56,160 · p < 0.001
53 × 1,081 categories

Machine Group × Product Code

V = 0.591
Strong association
χ² = 885,616 · dof = 24,128 · p < 0.001
53 × 465 categories

Machine Group × Interruption Level

V = 0.371
Moderate association
χ² = 20,208 · dof = 156 · p < 0.001
53 × 4 categories

Reason codes and product codes are both very strongly tied to which machine group is stopped — expected, since each machine group runs its own equipment-specific fault vocabulary and product mix. The weaker (but still significant) link to Interruption Level shows that how severe a stoppage is classified is more evenly spread across machines than why it happens.

03 — THREE-WAY STRUCTURE (MULTIPLE CORRESPONDENCE ANALYSIS)

Combining three variables at once

MCA extends the same idea to three categorical variables simultaneously, projecting every category onto a shared 2-D map based on how often (by count) each combination of categories co-occurs. Four three-way models were built in addition to the master model in §4. For each, this report lists all three of that file's top-5 tables: the highest-interruption-time combinations, the highest-lift combinations, and the closest category pairs on the MCA map.

05 — FINDINGS & RECOMMENDATIONS

What this means for the floor

  1. Two process families cause most of the interruption time. Wire bonding (WB-KS, WB-ASM) and die attach (DS-DISCO, DA-ESEC, DA-ASM) together account for over half of all logged interruption time, and "DC=Short stop" is their single most frequent recurring reason code across nearly every top-5 table in this report — a classic micro-stop signature worth attacking with SMED/andon-response tooling rather than a full overhaul.
  2. A subset of machine groups is almost entirely Critical-level. OVEN-ATV (99.9%), HDLR-MULTITEST (99.5%), HDLR-IN2 (99.5%), CLNR-MARCH (99.3%) and HDLR-MCT (99.4%) show almost no low/medium-level interruptions at all. These are the best candidates for predictive maintenance, since nearly every recorded event is severe.
  3. Several fault codes are machine-exclusive fingerprints, not shared causes. Every closest-pairs table in this report agrees: reason code "514" belongs only to INSP-CAMTEK; "MOLD STATION" belongs only to MOLD-FICO; "CHANGE CAPILLARY" and "OUTPUT ELEVATOR" belong only to WB-ORTHODYNE. These surface consistently at both the Machine Group and the individual Machine ID level, confirming they're equipment idiosyncrasies to fix at the machine, not systemic process issues.
  4. Machine–product coupling is strong (V=0.591). Several machines are effectively dedicated to a single product family (e.g. BLU-MIRAE ↔ 1635705-4C-C$KH), so interruptions attributed to "the machine" may really be attributable to that specific product's process window — worth separating in future root-cause reviews.
  5. Interruption Level is only moderately tied to Machine Group (V=0.371). Unlike reason code and product, how severe a stoppage is classified is comparatively machine-agnostic — suggesting severity is driven more by the nature of the specific fault than by which machine group experiences it.
  6. Extreme lift values point to root causes, not noise. Every lift table in this report surfaces combinations occurring from ~3,700x up to ~1.9 million times more often than random chance predicts. Because the underlying counts are small (5–20 events), these won't move total interruption-time rankings, but they are the cleanest possible evidence that a specific machine, reason and product are mechanically linked.
